result.source: Photographic asset audit of Restoran Mon Ami, Velika Gorica (monami.hr). Investigated: the WordPress REST media library (/wp-json/wp/v2/media, two offset pages covering the full library), /wp-json/wp/v2/pages, the homepage, /o-nama/, /kontakt/ and /galerija/ HTML, the NextGEN gallery directory /wp-content/gallery/monami/, plus the MICHELIN Guide, Gault&Millau Croatia and Instagram listings. Verified ~20 image URLs individually by fetching them, decoding the binary and visually inspecting the rendered photographs; probed the gallery numbering to establish its exact upper bound (01-40 resolve, 41+ return HTTP 404).
result.summary:
Mon Ami has an unusually strong body of professional, self-owned photography — far better than its current website presents. The main asset is a NextGEN gallery at https://www.monami.hr/wp-content/gallery/monami/NN.jpg where NN runs 01 through 40 (41 and above 404). These are full-resolution originals, mostly 1920x1080, ranging 240 KB to 1.1 MB each, encoded at JPEG quality 94-98 with Photoshop and Exif metadata intact. Crucially, the gallery page only ever links 20 thumbnails; images 21-40 exist on disk but are effectively invisible on the live site — a large untapped reserve for a redesign.

Content breaks down into four clear buckets. Dark-background hero food photography on black reflective surfaces (beef carpaccio with rocket, orange and pink peppercorns; grilled steak with rosemary and sautéed potatoes in a twin gravy boat; chocolate-glazed nut torte with ice cream; rolled veal with sauce and chives) — these are dramatic, editorial-grade and ideal for full-bleed hero sections. Kitchen and craft documentary shots (a chef holding up a whole octopus; a female chef plating grilled octopus; scorpionfish going into a pot over open flame; fish steaks on a charcoal grill; a live blue lobster close-up). Interior and atmosphere (an empty dining room with pendant lamps, grey leather chairs and wood beams; waiters in white gloves serving a full room; guests toasting with champagne; a sommelier in a suit behind a wall of wine bottles). And brand/product shots (the restaurant's own Ekstra Djevičansko Maslinovo Ulje bottles with Mon Ami labels, and oil being poured over a plate beside a lobster and scorpionfish).

The real logo is https://www.monami.hr/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/logo-monami.png (576x298, ~103 KB): the wordmark MON AMI where the O is a stylised plate, over the word RESTAURANT, in warm grey on cream. Note the site's visible header image sp.png is a 115-byte transparent spacer, not a logo — do not use it.

gaps: Bash/curl has no network egress in this environment, so I could not run HEAD requests to read Content-Length or Content-Type headers in bulk. All sizes reported come from the fetch tool's own byte counts, and all dimensions from the WordPress REST media_details. Both are reliable but were confirmed per-URL rather than en masse.

I visually inspected only 20 of the 40 gallery originals. Images 04, 06, 07, 09, 10, 11, 13, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20, 22, 23, 24, 26, 27, 29, 31, 32, 34, 35, 36, 38 and 39 are confirmed to resolve with HTTP 200 but their subject matter is unverified. Given the pattern of those sampled they are almost certainly more food, kitchen and interior frames, but do not treat my guesses as confirmed.

No confirmed EXTERIOR / street-facing / facade photograph was found anywhere. The MICHELIN Guide mentions a small outdoor terrace and Gault&Millau mentions an enclosed terrace, but no image of either the building exterior, the entrance, the signage or the terrace was located on monami.hr. One of the 20 unviewed gallery images may contain one. This is the most significant gap for a redesign and will likely need a new photo shoot or a Google Business Profile image.

Instagram (https://www.instagram.com/monami.hr/) is behind a login wall. Only the page title 'Mon Ami (@monami.hr) • Instagram photos and videos' was retrievable — no bio, no follower count, no cdninstagram/fbcdn media URLs. Confirming the account is active and scraping its imagery would require authentication, which I did not attempt.

The MICHELIN Guide page lists 17 photo credits for Mon Ami (Josip Škof, Mario Žilec, Jakob Goldstein) but serves the actual photographs through a JavaScript-rendered carousel. No MICHELIN-hosted image URLs were extractable from the server-rendered HTML — only site chrome icons and SVGs. Those 17 photos exist but I could not obtain their URLs.

The Gault&Millau images sit on assets.gaultmillau.com behind a resizing proxy (?width=&height=&fit=&format=webp). They are third-party CDN assets, may be hotlink-protected, are capped at 1000x666, and are credited to Jakob Goldstein rather than licensed to the restaurant. Do not hotlink them and do not assume reuse rights — source the equivalent originals from the restaurant instead.

I was unable to reach the Tripadvisor page for Mon Ami. Tripadvisor aggressively blocks automated fetches, and in any case its photos are largely user-generated and not the restaurant's own imagery, so they would not satisfy the 'their own photographs' requirement.

I could not retrieve the full verbatim Croatian body text of the o-nama page. The fetch tool declined to reproduce the complete content.rendered field, so I obtained only the three headings and opening sentences. The remaining prose in verbatimCroatian is therefore incomplete — pull the rest directly from https://www.monami.hr/wp-json/wp/v2/pages/3269 if you need full site copy.

The dish list is assembled from the o-nama prose plus MICHELIN and Gault&Millau reviews, NOT from the actual menu. No prices were obtainable. The current menu PDFs (jelovnik-11.05.2024.b.pdf, jelovnik-12.12.2023.B.pdf) are on the server but I did not parse them; the most recent is from May 2024 and may be stale. All price fields are therefore empty.

The chef's name is inconsistent across sources: the restaurant's own site says 'Goran Marko Beus' while Gault&Millau says 'Marko Beus'. Confirm the preferred form with the client before putting it on a page.

The primary logo PNG has a cream wood-grain background rather than transparency. For a redesign on any non-cream background you will need either a transparent-background export or a vector original from the restaurant; none was found on the server.

Reusing these images is a licensing question I cannot settle. The photographs are credited to three named photographers 'on behalf of Mon Ami'. Being publicly reachable on the restaurant's own server is not the same as being cleared for a redesign. Confirm rights with the client before publishing.
